security_audit.summary: The flagged items are Markdown examples and reference material, not executable skill code. Package commands, Azure credential environment variable names, private IP allowlist examples, and official links are legitimate documentation patterns with no evidence of exfiltration or prompt injection. No semantic security finding was identified.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples trigger external command heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Label installation commands as user-run setup examples and avoid implying automatic execution by the agent.

remediation.issue: Credential environment variable examples include a client secret placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short warning that placeholder secret values must never be committed, logged, or pasted into prompts.

remediation.issue: Private IP allowlist examples may be copied without review.
remediation.suggestion: State that IP ranges are examples only and must be replaced with approved environment-specific ranges.

content.user_title: Manage Azure Durable Task Schedulers in .NET
content.value_statement: Provisioning Durable Task Scheduler resources through Azure Resource Manager requires exact SDK patterns. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise .NET guidance for schedulers, task hubs, retention policies, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Lists the packages needed for Azure Resource Manager Durable Task and Azure Identity.
Shows DefaultAzureCredential setup with subscription and resource group access.
Demonstrates scheduler creation with Dedicated and Consumption SKU options.
Covers task hub, retention policy, list, update, get, and delete workflows.
Explains the boundary between management-plane and data-plane Durable Task SDKs.
limitations: Does not run Azure commands or validate cloud resources by itself.
Does not replace Azure permissions, quota, pricing, or compliance review.
Examples use placeholder names and private IP ranges that require environment-specific changes.
Version information should be checked against current Azure SDK releases before production use.

use_cases.title: Provision Scheduler Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Create Durable Task Scheduler resources, task hubs, and retention policies with Azure Resource Manager SDK patterns.

use_cases.title: Select the Correct SDK Layer
use_cases.description: Confirm when to use management-plane APIs instead of data-plane Durable Task client or worker packages.

use_cases.title: Review Lifecycle Operations
use_cases.description: Check create, update, list, get, and delete flows before adding resource management code to a service.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the SDK Boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain whether I should use Azure.ResourceManager.DurableTask or a data-plane Durable Task SDK for my task.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Scheduler Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a .NET Durable Task Scheduler deployment with resource group, scheduler, SKU, and task hub choices.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Lifecycle Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Create guidance for adding create, list, update, get, and delete operations for Durable Task Scheduler resources in .NET.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Durable Task Scheduler management approach for authentication, idempotency, IP allowlists, cleanup order, and error handling.

output_examples.input: I need to create a Durable Task Scheduler and task hub with the management-plane SDK.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the ARM Durable Task package, recommends DefaultAzureCredential, outlines scheduler creation, adds a task hub, and includes cleanup guidance.

output_examples.input: I am unsure whether this SDK starts orchestrations.
output_examples.output: The response explains that this SDK manages Azure resources. It directs orchestration start and query work to the data-plane Durable Task SDK.

output_examples.input: Review my retention policy and deletion flow.
output_examples.output: The response checks retention policy placement, long-running operation handling, task hub deletion order, and resource group assumptions.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and keep service principal secrets outside source control.
Use idempotent create-or-update flows for repeatable infrastructure changes.
Delete task hubs before deleting their scheduler resources.
anti_patterns: Using management-plane APIs to start, query, or signal orchestration instances.
Hardcoding tenant, client, subscription, or secret values in application code.
Copying sample IP allowlists or resource names into production without review.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps use the Azure Resource Manager Durable Task SDK for scheduler, task hub, and retention policy management.

faq.question: Can it start Durable Task orchestrations?
faq.answer: No. Starting or querying orchestrations belongs to the data-plane Durable Task client SDK.

faq.question: Which authentication approach does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes DefaultAzureCredential, which supports local development and managed Azure identity scenarios.

faq.question: Does it include production-ready infrastructure values?
faq.answer: No. Resource names, regions, SKUs, and IP ranges are examples that must be reviewed for each environment.

faq.question: Is this only for .NET projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples and APIs focus on the .NET Azure Resource Manager SDK.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
